description: I am a Software Engineering student and full-stack AI developer building Orbisys for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Orbisys uses live NASA satellite datasets (EONET & Earth Observatory) to visualize and analyze global environmental trends—like wildfires, storms, and climate anomalies—into clear, actionable insights. Open to connecting with contributors in Earth Science, Data Visualization, or AI/ML.
summary: Orbisys is an interactive Earth observation and climate trend intelligence platform built for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. While NASA satellites continuously capture critical environmental anomalies, raw telemetry feeds and coordinate logs can be difficult for students, researchers, and local communities to interpret quickly. Orbisys solves this by connecting directly to NASA’s live Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker (EONET v3) API and visualizing active global hazards—wildfires, severe storms, volcanic activity, and sea/lake ice shifts—on an interactive 3D wireframe dotted globe. Users can compare anomaly frequencies across 7-day, 30-day, and 90-day observation windows, inspect orbital pass persistence, and generate instant Earth System Trend Synthesis dossiers with exact coordinates and sensor context. By turning complex orbital feeds into clear visual insights, Orbisys empowers faster environmental awareness and climate trend analysis.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Orbisys is a real-time mission-control web console designed for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. It fetches live, keyless telemetry directly from NASA’s Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker (EONET v3) REST API and plots active natural events onto a custom interactive 3D orthographic dotted-matrix Earth globe. When a user selects an event from the live telemetry stream or clicks a glowing hazard marker on the globe, the camera smoothly rotates and locks onto the event's exact latitude and longitude while opening an "Earth System Trend Synthesis" dossier.

Key Features & Capabilities:

1. Interactive 3D Dotted Globe: Built with D3.js orthographic projection and HTML5 Canvas, displaying global landmasses, graticules, drag-to-rotate controls, scroll-to-zoom, and color-coded pulsing hazard pins (Wildfires, Severe Storms, Volcanoes, and Sea & Lake Ice).

2. Multi-Window Trend Detective (7D / 30D / 90D): Allows users to switch observation horizons to compare active anomaly counts, category percentage shares, and regional clustering over time.

3. Trend Analytics & Orbital Persistence: Ranks active global events by sequential satellite observation passes (persistence metrics) so users can distinguish short-lived thermal events from long-term cryospheric shifts such as tracked Antarctic icebergs.

4. Earth System Trend Synthesis Dossier: Provides domain-specific scientific context referencing orbital detection instruments (such as MODIS Terra/Aqua and VIIRS 375m thermal bands), reported magnitudes, timestamps, and direct verification links to official NASA event sources.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Raw satellite datasets often create a barrier between open space data and everyday decision-making. Orbisys bridges this gap by offering an intuitive, zero-latency visual interface that helps students, educators, journalists, and local responders spot emerging regional climate patterns and understand the physical environmental drivers behind them.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & Framework: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons

- Geospatial & Data Visualization: D3.js (d3-geo orthographic projection & geoDistance visibility culling), HTML5 Canvas, Natural Earth 110m GeoJSON

- Live Data & Hosting: NASA EONET v3 API, GitHub, Vercel

Creativity & Design Considerations:

Instead of presenting static tables or heavy WebGL textures that can fail on low-bandwidth devices, we engineered a lightweight, 60fps dark-mode mission-control interface centered around a high-contrast halftone dotted globe. Every visual element—from hazard color coding to synchronized fly-to animations—was designed to keep focus on spatial and temporal Earth system trends.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure:

Live satellite event telemetry is sourced directly from NASA Open Data (EONET v3). Generative AI / Super Intelligence (SI) tools were used to assist with frontend UI scaffolding, code structuring, and drafting descriptive documentation.
